bull.b: Autoship making ~84% of sales and growing >10% YoY creates a durable, subscription-like revenue base. High penetration boosts order frequency, predictability, and retention, supporting long-term cash flow visibility, lower acquisition economics per sale, and steadier margin conversion.

Consistent FCF provides durable internal funding for clinic rollouts, M&A, share repurchases and working capital, reducing reliance on capital markets. Robust cash generation improves resilience to cyclical demand and enables gradual deleveraging or strategic investment without eroding operations.

Meaningful EBITDA margin expansion and >25% flow‑through show operating leverage from SG&A discipline, pricing and mix. Structural margin improvement, if sustained, supports durable profitability even with modest revenue growth and funds reinvestment in growth initiatives.

bear.b: Operating and net margins near low single digits leave little buffer against input-cost inflation, logistics or promotional pressure. For a retailer, this structural thinness increases earnings volatility and makes multi-quarter margin sustainability sensitive to execution and cyclical demand shifts.

bear.t: Moderate leverage for a low-margin retailer
bear.b: Meaningful leverage amplifies downside risk for a company with thin margins. Even with ample liquidity, debt servicing and incremental interest (including a new term loan) constrain capital flexibility, limit aggressive reinvestment, and raise sensitivity to rising rates or weaker cash conversion.

bear.t: Slower customer net adds and attach-rate pressure
bear.b: A slower pace of new-customer acquisition and softer premiumization/attach rates constrains long-term revenue growth and limits expansion of NSPAC. Reduced top-line momentum makes it harder to scale fixed costs and realize projected returns from clinic and service investments.
